transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-03-04 14:00 UTC
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Marta Alvarez (Cynosure Head of AI), Ben Cho (Infra Lead), Samir Patel (Data Privacy)

Summary:
Cynosure is evaluating moving production inference off OpenAI to a Dedicated Redwood deployment for cost, latency, and data control reasons. They run a mix of generation and reranking workloads; heavy peak QPS around product launches. Primary concerns: model compatibility (we use vLLM/TGI internally for some workloads), eval parity (outputs must match or exceed current OpenAI quality), SOC2/KMS/SSO requirements, and effort to migrate prompts and safety checks.

Topics: pricing vs TCO, Dedicated capacity sizing, compat with vLLM/TGI and HuggingFace models, eval harness, private/VPC options, audit logs and key management.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account, with Priya our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Marta: Good thanks, Marta here. Quick context, we currently run most inference on OpenAI for chat and summarization, but costs have spiked and we need more control for data residency and auditability.
[00:15] Ben: Hi, Ben here. We also run an internal vLLM/TGI stack for some experimental flows. We want to understand compatibility and if we can reuse artifacts.
[00:23] Priya: Awesome, thanks. We'll cover high-level Redwood Dedicated, migration patterns, and then dig into compatibility with vLLM/TGI and eval parity — and SOC2/KMS questions at the end. Does that sound right?
[00:31] Samir: Yes, also want to confirm SSO and logs — security is a hard stop for us.

[00:45] Jordan: Quick question on scale — what's your current monthly token spend and peak QPS?
[00:50] Marta: Ballpark 1.2B tokens/month, spikes to ~600 RPS during launches, average seq length 300 tokens. That number bounces around.
[01:02] Ben: Most traffic is generation for chat and also a reranking pipeline that hits shorter contexts but high QPS.

[01:15] Priya: Ok, that's helpful. For Dedicated we typically size pools based on throughput needs and latency SLOs; you can pin model versions and we provide autoscaling. On the model side — can you clarify which models you use via OpenAI and which you run on vLLM/TGI?
[01:31] Marta: OpenAI mostly GPT-4o and gpt-4.1 for higher-quality outputs. vLLM/TGI runs smaller open models for cost-sensitive tasks and internal reranking. We also experiment with Claude for a couple of flows.
[01:45] Jordan: Great, the migration path depends on whether you want exact parity vs acceptable divergence. For some workloads you can switch to Redwood-hosted variants of open models with tuned prompts; for others you'll want to run the same model archive — we support loading HF checkpoints and common TGI artifacts.

[02:03] Ben: When you say support TGI artifacts, do you mean we can drop in the same config and it will behave the same? Because we saw differences between vLLM and TGI in kv cache handling and temperature defaults.
[02:18] Priya: Good point. We try to support model format compat and provide runtime knobs to match kv-cache behavior and decoding defaults. There's often subtle differences — that's why we recommend running an eval parity harness. We'll help you set that up.

[02:35] Marta: Can you run benchmarks using our real prompts? We need to validate quality is at least equal and not degraded by quantization or different kernels.
[02:44] Priya: Absolutely. Typical approach: we take a representative prompt set, run n generates on your current provider (OpenAI), run on Redwood Dedicated with your chosen model/quantization profile, and compare metrics — BLEU/ROUGE-ish where applicable, and human eval samples. We'll also surface latency and cost per token.

[03:05] Jordan: On pricing, Dedicated is committed capacity — monthly contract — but we can show a migration TCO vs pay-as-you-go OpenAI. In many cases customers pay back within a few months if their usage is high. We'll send a TCO sheet.
[03:19] Ben: How do you handle model updates and rollouts? We like canary deploys for models with controlled ramp.
[03:27] Priya: We have rollout controls: canary, A/B, automatic fallback to a cheaper variant if latency SLOs break. You pin model versions and define route policies.

[03:40] Samir: Security stuff — SOC2, KMS, audit logs, SSO. Can Dedicated run in our VPC and use our KMS?
[03:49] Jordan: Yes, Redwood Private/Dedicated supports customer-managed networking and KMS/HSM integrations. We'll share the security pack, SOC2 attestation, and a guide on KMS setup.
[03:59] Marta: Do you retain any customer data on the host side? We need no-logs or configurable retention.
[04:05] Priya: You can configure retention; for Dedicated we offer options with zero-persist modes and audit logs forwarded to your SIEM. We'll share specifics.

[04:20] Ben: Back to vLLM and TGI — a couple of our datasets require exact tokenization/stop sequence behavior. Are there known mismatch issues?
[04:30] Priya: Tokenization is usually consistent if you're using the same tokenizer model, but decoding and stop handling can differ. We'll provide runtime flags to emulate common behaviors and show the mapping in our docs; sometimes you need small prompt adjustments.

[04:45] Marta: Any customers who've moved from OpenAI to Redwood Dedicated and kept parity?
[04:50] Jordan: Yes — a few finserv and commerce customers. We did a case study (link provided during call) showing eval parity for xFlow and 10–15% lower cost on average. I'll send the reference.

[05:05] Ben: What's the integration effort — do we need to rework our orchestration around vLLM?
[05:12] Priya: Minimal if you use the Redwood API — it's a drop-in replacing host endpoint calls. If you want to run models by archive in your Dedicated pool we help with packaging. For our runtime, we handle KV cache and batching.
[05:30] Marta: Are there constraints on model size or sequence length for Dedicated? Our longest context is ~8k tokens on few workloads.
[05:38] Priya: We support large-context models and have kernel selection tuned for long seqs; for very long contexts you may need higher GPU memory instances. We'll size the pool accordingly.
[05:50] Jordan: Quick pause — any regulatory constraints on where workloads must run? EU data residency, etc?
[05:55] Marta: We'd prefer EU for EU customers, US for US. Some clients require on-prem in certain cases.
[06:03] Jordan: We support region-pin and Private on-prem installs for air-gapped needs.

[06:15] Samir: On the eval side, can Redwood help automate A/B comparisons and track quality regressions over time?
[06:24] Priya: Yes — Redwood Optimize includes eval suites, prompt set regression alerts, and tie-ins to the console to watch quality metrics per rollout. We integrate human eval workflows too.

[06:40] Marta: How about function/tool calling and streaming? We rely on streaming for UX.
[06:45] Jordan: Streaming is supported on all modes; function/tool calling patterns are supported — we'll demo in the tech deep dive.

[06:55] Ben: For our TGI runs we use custom CUDA kernels sometimes; will that be supported?
[07:02] Priya: We can't run arbitrary customer CUDA in the managed runtime, but if you have a known model/kernel combo we can evaluate adding support or provide private deployment where you control runtimes.

[07:15] Marta: Ok. Next, SLA expectations and maintenance windows — we need SLAs for latency and uptime.
[07:23] Jordan: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and target latency tiers in enterprise contracts. We'll include SLA terms in the proposal.

[07:35] Priya: I'd like to propose the following technical next steps: 1) Cynosure sends 1-week representative prompt set and traffic profile; 2) Redwood runs an eval parity run on a small Dedicated pool using your top models; 3) joint review of results and iteration.
[07:52] Marta: That sounds good. What kind of artifacts will you need?
[07:56] Priya: Sample prompts, expected QPS, sequence lengths, current provider responses (for baseline), and a small safety policy doc if you have custom filters.

[08:10] Ben: Is there a sandbox Dedicated we can try before commit? We prefer to validate perf with our traffic.
[08:17] Jordan: We can provision a short-term trial Dedicated or run a hosted pilot with traffic replay to mimic your load — depends on how isolated you want the environment. We'll propose options in the follow-up.

[08:30] Samir: On compliance, please send SOC2 and privacy whitepaper. Also SSO SAML integration doc.
[08:37] Jordan: We'll attach the security pack and connect you with the security team. Link: https://redwood.example.com/security (will send via email).

[08:48] Marta: One last question on cost — do you have guidance on quantization tradeoffs for parity vs cost reduction?
[08:55] Priya: Yes — our Optimize team recommends quant profiles per model and workload. In many cases 4-bit quant can reduce costs significantly with small quality delta, but for critical flows we recommend FP16 or INT8. We'll include recommendation table in the TCO.

[09:15] Jordan: Okay let's recap quick. Action items: Jordan sends pricing/TCO and case studies; Priya shares benchmark harness and requests prompt set; Cynosure provides prompts and traffic. We'll schedule a tech deep-dive next week. Anything else?
[09:32] Marta: No, that's it — thanks.
[09:35] Jordan: Thanks all, we'll follow up with notes and links.

[09:40] -- end main call --

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hear: "dedcated" or "v-L M" appear in automated text, some filler words removed. There was short crosstalk around 02:30 where Ben interrupted Priya about TGI specifics; small overlap.
